correctness.rationale: Cyclic binary differencing forbids exactly 100 and 111 on the difference bits, including the repeated-coordinate tests for small n. A nonzero vector therefore consists of one- or two-one runs separated by single zeros. With t ones it has k=n−t zeros and s=2t−n long blocks. Marking a zero gives n binom(k,s) placements; dividing by k counts indexed vectors even if they have a smaller least period. Cyclic integration has exactly two solutions when t is even and none otherwise; the zero vector gives two constants. This proves the full coefficient formula. The two parity trace terms have determinants (1−z)(1∓uz²−u²z³), giving both generating functions and the stated initial counts. Möbius inversion handles primitive orbits. Besides the positive root λ of x³−x−1, the two conjugate roots have modulus λ^(−1/2)<1. For x³+x−1 the real root ρ lies in (0.68,1), so the conjugate roots have modulus ρ^(−1/2)<1.22. Proper-divisor terms are O(n λ^(n/2)), proving the growth statements. For entropy, every admissible finite difference block extends in both directions in the difference-state graph and has two extendible binary lifts; this gives the same block growth rate and entropy log λ. The unmodified support script was inspected, not executed. A separate bounded check tested the original periodic condition and counted transitions for all 32,766 binary words through length 14, agreeing with the formula. Reproduction is to iterate n=1..14 and masks 0..2^n−1, test all n modular comparisons, histogram unequal cyclic neighbors, and compare with exact binomial arithmetic; no replay file was retained. The infinite assertions rest on the proof, not this finite check.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Left-multiplication of the given T± by diag(1,u,u) records transitions, while the two constant self-loops contribute weight 1 each. The weighted determinants are 1−uz²−u²z³ and 1+uz²−u²z³. The formal logarithmic derivative is the asserted bivariate series. Expanding the two negative logarithms gives (uz²+u²z³)^k/k and (−uz²+u²z³)^k/k before applying z∂z. A term z^n u^t has k=n−t and s=2t−n; the two signs enforce even parity and give 2n binom(k,s)/k. Thus the transition-resolved expression is a direct marked-edge specialization of the explicit indexed instance, not just of an abstract existence theorem.
